<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

Cross-model review of s123: a message is delivered exactly once to a pi/omp seat. READ-ONLY. Your question is the MECHANISM, not whether the coder applied it neatly. The coder already killed one prime-approved design by testing it (daemon claim-before-publish stole rows from waiting inbox readers) — assume the same rigour and go after what it could not see from inside its own fix.

<a id="instructions"></a>

## Instructions

- Read plan.dd.md, impl-guide.dd.md, assets/live-delivery-transcripts.md, assets/ac-2-prefx-red.md, then the branch diff
- PRIORITY 1 — ordering and failure paths: claim→inject→ack. Prove for yourself that a FAILED inject cannot ack (body must redeliver), and that an empty claim suppresses injection rather than injecting stale or nothing-shaped data
- PRIORITY 2 — the six daemon inbox guards that killed design #1 must still be green AND still meaningful: check they were not weakened to fit the new design
- PRIORITY 3 — cross-runtime seam: inbox-claim.wire.json is meant to stop the field-spelling drift that has bitten this repo repeatedly. Verify BOTH sides actually consume it rather than restating the shape; a wire artifact nobody reads is worse than none
- PRIORITY 4 — version skew both directions (old extension/new daemon, new extension/old daemon): no silent body loss, no double-ack, and the failure that does occur must be LOUD
- The live transcripts are evidence: check they show what they claim (one rendering, queue row terminal-acked), not merely that something arrived
- Report findings to the PRIME (pij-still-weasel), never sideways to the coder. Verdict: APPROVE or findings with severity.
